subject: operating-systems
title: Scheduling metrics and trade-offs
summary: Scheduling metrics quantify responsiveness, completion efficiency, and fairness rather than identifying one universally optimal policy.

questions.prompt: Turnaround time is measured from which two events?
options: Creation of a file to deletion
questions.answerKey: Turnaround time is completion time minus arrival time.
questions.explanation: It includes both waiting and execution time.

questions.prompt: What does response time measure for an interactive request?
options: Time until its first CPU service/response
questions.answerKey: Response time measures how long until the task first receives service or produces an initial response.
questions.explanation: It differs from turnaround, which waits for completion.

questions.prompt: A job arrives at 2 ms and starts at 7 ms. What is its waiting time before first execution?
questions.answerKey: Waiting before its first execution is 7 - 2 = 5 ms.
questions.explanation: Additional preempted ready-queue time may be counted in total waiting depending on the metric definition.

questions.prompt: Why can maximizing throughput hurt interactive response time?
options: Throughput and response time are identical
Batching long jobs can keep the processor busy while delaying short interactive jobs
Interactive jobs cannot be scheduled preemptively
questions.answerKey: A policy optimized for completed jobs per unit time may delay first service for interactive work.

questions.prompt: Define waiting time, turnaround time, and response time.
questions.answerKey: Waiting time is time spent in the ready queue; turnaround time is completion minus arrival; response time is first service/response minus arrival.

questions.prompt: Explain one trade-off between a small and a large round-robin quantum.
questions.answerKey: A small quantum improves responsiveness and fairness but causes more context-switch overhead. A large quantum reduces switching overhead and improves CPU efficiency for bursts, but can make interactive tasks wait longer and approach FCFS behavior.
questions.explanation: The best quantum depends on workload and switch cost.
